objective_result.summary: The baseline fully revalidated retained-claim packages after targeted repair, including 19 claim identities whose compared identity fields stayed unchanged across all three validation passes. Incremental reuse is implemented with fail-closed identity and prompt-context checks. The repair-bearing candidate used fewer grounding calls but had longer end-to-end latency; a corrected candidate passed quality but did not exercise repair.

provider_call_trace.interpretation_limit: The retained profile records stage, request, and timing metadata but not rendered request bodies. It proves full-package validation repeated unchanged claim identities and that five grounding stages ran in each pass; it cannot establish that every one of the ten repair-pass requests was wholly redundant.

baseline_validation_trace.legacy_identity_limit: The baseline package predates provenance_hash and retrieval identity fields. The listed comparison uses all identity-bearing fields present in those artifacts. No legacy package is eligible for reuse by the new implementation; missing current identity fields trigger full validation.

candidate_runs.label: repair_bearing_candidate_before_readiness_gate_fix
candidate_runs.readiness_gate_correction: Commit 6bf4cd48 accepts semantic execution identity schema 1.1 only when its retrieval identity is a valid SHA-256, while retaining schema 1.0 support. The candidate run itself remains recorded as readiness-failed under the then-current gate.

candidate_runs.label: corrected_candidate_no_repair
candidate_runs.interpretation: This confirms end-to-end quality under the corrected gate, but it does not measure repair-path reuse because no targeted repair occurred.

identity_components: report, source, validator, configuration, and policy identity
retrieval, model, prompt-family, and execution identity
exact rendered batch prompt content hash
reuse_contract.removed_claims: Do not carry prior results forward
reuse_contract.final_package_and_readiness: Merge deterministic reused and new results, then run the existing complete-package validation and readiness gates.

telemetry.limitation: The frozen runner retains provider usage and workflow databases but not structured application log events. Therefore actual per-run reuse counters could not be recovered from these runs; provider call totals are reported separately and are not attributed solely to reuse.

performance_conclusion.repair_bearing_comparison: Control report_analysis was 388.688 s and repair-bearing candidate was 430.922 s (+42.234 s). Report wall was 483.348 s versus 512.148 s (+28.800 s). Grounding calls fell from 15 to 8 and grounding provider-active wall fell from 137.793 s to 118.260 s, but report-analysis provider-active wall increased from 372.275 s to 413.137 s. This run does not demonstrate a latency reduction.
performance_conclusion.cost_comparison: Control cost was $0.108506 and repair-bearing candidate cost was $0.090994. The corrected no-repair candidate cost $0.077599, but its different repair workload makes that result unsuitable as repair-path evidence.
performance_conclusion.decision: Keep the safe reuse implementation because unchanged full-package revalidation was demonstrated and local correctness regressions pass. Do not claim a speedup from these runs.

next_recommendation: Retain the existing reuse-decision event in the frozen-run evidence path, without adding a telemetry service, then use a preselected frozen report known to repair for a single corrected candidate run. Compare claim-level reuse counters and provider intervals before concluding that repair-path latency improved.
